messages:
Aria (marketing): Quick sync  we need a compact battlecard + 90s webinar blurb for next Wed. Angle: serving economics vs cloud endpoints and infra vendors.
Ben (sales): Field signals: customers ask about surprise bills, p99 spikes, and migration effort. Need 1-line rebuttals.
Tessa (product): Structure: claim, why it matters (plain), demo hook. Keep language non-technical for execs + 1 micro-technical line for SREs.
Ravi (eng): Bench note: internal dialbench shows ~2x median token cost reduction with KV prefix cache + batching vs a major cloud endpoint in our lab. Will avoid p99 claims.
Aria (marketing): Draft hero lines (pick one):
 - "Keep your models, fix your inference economics."
 - "Serve smarter: lower bills, steady latency."
Ben (sales): First rebut pair: "We're on CloudA already" -> "CloudA is great for prototypes. At scale teams face opaque billing and tail latency; Redwood adds routing, caching and fallbacks to make costs and latency predictable."
Tessa (product): SRE micro-line: "Continuous batching, per-session KV prefix reuse, and model-variant fallbacks reduce repeated compute for common prompts."
Ravi (eng): Tiny routing snippet for slide:
```json
{"policy":"latency-first","fallbacks":["lite-quant"],"batch_ms":10}
```
Aria (marketing): Inbound routing rules (simple):
 - Keywords -> AE: "SLA, on-prem, private, dedicated"
 - Keywords -> SDR: "trial, api key, embed, free credits"
 - Score >=80 -> AE outreach, 50-79 -> SDR, <50 -> nurture
asset-bot: Created asset stub https://internal.redwood/marketing/assets/serve-econ-mini (editing: marketing)
Ben (sales): I'll draft two roleplay rebut lines and drop here after Aria posts the one-pager.
Aria (marketing): Thanks  aiming to freeze copy by EOD Monday so design can mock the slide. If you have sharper wording, post now.
